label: Viral
about: Built to hold attention: your strongest line first, no dead air, slightly faster pace, bold word-by-word captions and something new on screen every few seconds.
editor_notes: Judgement pass, because the automatic version only sees words. (1) The first 1-3 seconds decide everything: open on a specific claim, number, result or question, with a 2-5 word hook title that adds to the line rather than repeating it. Replace the automatic teaser if a better line exists, or remove it if the opening is already strong. (2) One idea per video; cut anything that doesn't serve it, aiming for 20-45 s. (3) Something should change on screen every 2-4 s: a zoom, graphic, sticker or B-roll, but never on top of the payoff line. (4) End on the payoff with no fade or sign-off, so it can loop. (5) Don't promise views: this improves the odds of holding attention, and the idea matters more than the edit.
